ch01.before: Zhang Huichong was a legend of the Chinese screen
ch01.alt: Two black-and-white photographs: at left, the magician and film star Zhang Huichong holding a large crystal ball with a woman's face reflected inside it; at right, a stage tableau of his Shanghai-style magic act, performers in Chinese costume beside a latticed cabinet.
ch01.caption: Zhang Huichong (left) and his Shanghai-style magic in performance (right), which once swept Republican-era Shanghai.

ch01.before: But on November 14, 1927, the Provisional Central Politburo held
ch01.alt: An organizational tree diagram. At the top, a box labeled 'Provisional Central Politburo' enclosing 'Standing Committee.' Below, flanked by the Party Newspaper Committee at left and the Labor Movement Committee at right, a box labeled 'Organization Bureau.' Beneath it, a row of section boxes: Women's Movement Committee, Special-Service, Military, Publication-and-Distribution, Investigation, Propaganda, Organization, Accounts, Courier, and Secretariat.
ch01.caption: The Party's central structure after the reorganization of November 14, 1927, from Central Circular No. 17, "On the Party's Organizational Work."

ch08.before: Just then the renegade You Chongxin
ch08.alt: A photograph of a handwritten Chinese archival document, a ruled table listing arrested persons' names, dates and places of arrest, officers in charge, and dispositions.
ch08.caption: A case-list from the detection section of the Kuomintang's Wuhan field headquarters. First on this old file is You Chongxin (original name You Wuhun) who, before defecting and selling out Gu Shunzhang, had been a district Party secretary in Shanghai; the fourth entry, 'Hua Guangqi,' is annotated 'i.e. Gu Shunzhang.' (The caption renders the source's own.)
